q: An ergodic MPT T is called a K-automorphism (Kolmogorov automorphism) if there exists a sub-σ-algebra 𝒦 such that T⁻¹𝒦 ⊂ 𝒦, ∨ₙ T^n𝒦 = ℬ (full σ-algebra), and ∩ₙ T^{-n}𝒦 = {∅, X} (trivial tail). K-automorphisms satisfy:
opts: Completely positive entropy (h(T,𝒫) > 0 for every non-trivial 𝒫) and strong mixing
exp: K-systems (K-automorphisms): any K-system has completely positive entropy and is strongly mixing. The K-property lies between positive entropy and Bernoulli: all Bernoulli shifts are K, but not all K-systems are Bernoulli. K-systems are characterized by the 0-1 law for the tail field.
